column15: Tallest stills in Scotland; unpeated house style, well documented.

Eponymous Loch Lomond spirit is unpeated. The distillery also makes heavily peated siblings under other names (Inchmoan, Croftengea, not in this batch) - see brief's known-pairs list; only plain Loch Lomond is covered here.
~18-22ppm, roughly 75% peated / 25% unpeated malt.

Sources disagree: core range described both as unpeated/very lightly peated and as a union of peated and unpeated whiskies. Recorded light overall; Prophecy limited edition is heavily peated (see rule).

Numbered independent-bottler series by La Maison du Whisky (Paris), covering many distilleries worldwide incl. Karuizawa, Caol Ila, Macallan, Bowmore, Linkwood, Ardmore (all seen in samples). Peat varies per release; resolve via in-name distillery match.
Marketed as 'The Genuine Maritime Malt'; unpeated.
Core Spey range (Tenne, Royal Choice, etc.) is unpeated. 'Spey Fumare' (2016) was explicitly the distillery's first-ever peated release - see rule.
First modern single-barrel bourbon brand (1984). Brand legally owned by Age International Inc; produced/marketed by Sazerac at Buffalo Trace Distillery.

Genuine Scotch whisky (18 Highland/Speyside malts + Lowland grain) blended in Scotland for a French-owned company, best-seller in France; not a French-made whisky. No smoke/peat noted in flavour profile (vanilla, malt, oak). Blend spans regions so region left empty.
Lightly peated - easy to mis-assume 'none' for an ordinary-looking Speyside malt; sources are explicit that it is not fully unpeated.
Unpeated malt production; distinctive cooling-ring still design for a lighter style.
Blend of 15+ malts + Lowland grain by independent bottler/blender Charles Edge; no smoke/peat noted in any tasting note found.

Distillery spec explicitly lists 'Non peated' malt / 'Non peaty' new-make. Known for a distinctive waxy character unrelated to peat. Do not confuse with its historical neighbour Brora (a separate, distinct distillery with some heavily-peated years 1969-73) - Brora is not in this batch.

Split signal: the bulk blending-malt spirit is described as fully unpeated, but the official single malt (Deveron/Glen Deveron) is lightly peated ('gentle smokiness'). This batch's samples are independent-bottler single casks labelled 'Macduff' (incl. a Douglas Laing First Editions release), so the exact peat level of any given bottling is uncertain; recorded light out of caution rather than none. defaultTypeName left empty (range spans styles).
Retailer/producer copy mentions 'a gentle smoky note'; single non-technical source, low confidence.
Classic unpeated, rich Speyside style.
MGP Ingredients' first proprietary rye label (launched 2018), produced at their Lawrenceburg, Indiana distillery.

Family-run distillery on Achill Island, Co. Mayo, founded 2015. Makes both an unpeated core and a distinct 'Peated' single malt (see rule), plus single pot still - range spans types so defaultTypeName left empty.

London-based Elixir Distillers' rotating letter-coded range (since 2008) covering every Islay distillery. Peat varies by release/distillery - resolve via in-name match (e.g. Bowmore, seen in samples). See rule for the standalone permanent 'Peat' NAS expression.

Craft distillery in Three Oaks, Michigan (est. 2011); organic-grain bourbon and rye. No peat/smoke found in any product description; American craft grain whiskey, malted-barley peating essentially never used. defaultTypeName left empty (range spans bourbon/rye).

Pearse Lyons Distillery, Dublin (former St James' Church), opened 2017, founded by Dr Pearse Lyons. Range includes a blend ('Pearse Distillers Blend') alongside single malt/pot still releases, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat mentioned; Irish whiskey of this style is typically unpeated.

Annual Feis Ile release series from family-owned independent bottler Hunter Laing, mostly aged Islay single casks (Bowmore, Caol Ila, Bunnahabhain seen in this batch's samples; also historically Laphroaig, Ardbeg, Port Ellen). Peat varies by underlying distillery - resolve via in-name match.

Formerly 'Connacht Distillery' (Co. Mayo, est. 2015), rebranded Ballina in 2025 after acquisition by Terroirs Distillers (Tullibardine's owner). First releases Dubailte (double wood) and Triarach (triple wood), 100% Irish malted barley. No peat/smoke mentioned in sources found.

Glasgow distillery (Queen's Dock pumphouse), opened 2017. Core Stobcross/Napier releases are 'light, fruity and elegant' Lowland style. Distillery also makes a heavily peated once-a-year 'Fortnight' release (54ppm), not seen in this batch's samples - see rule.

Budget blend (20% malt content), produced in Scotland, mainly seen at retailers serving continental Europe. One retailer's tasting note explicitly mentions 'smoky and mineral notes' on the nose - treated as a light trace rather than none.

Tibetan Plateau single malt, matured in terracotta 'Jiu Hai' amphorae then finished in oak; 'Meido' and 'Craft White' are among its releases (both seen in samples). No ISO code for China/Tibet exists in the closed country list - used XX. No peat/smoke mentioned in any source found.

Okinawan awamori distiller (est. 1883) also producing pure-malt whisky and a blended whisky (Kaijin); range spans single malt and blend so defaultTypeName left empty. No smoke/peat in any tasting note found.
Bottled-in-Bond 100 proof rye, mashbill 51% rye / 37% corn / 12% malted barley. Historic Pennsylvania rye brand; Heaven Hill bought it in 1993.
Blended malt built on a Speyside signature malt + 16 others across regions; explicitly described as 'a base of un-peated core malts'.
Independent bottler's single-cask range; releases seen in samples are Teaninich and Blair Athol. Peat varies by underlying distillery - resolve via in-name match.
Single-product entry; whiskybase.com confirms the brand exists in its database but no identifying detail (origin, style, country) was found. Long-tail, fast-tracked per budget rules.

Historic Edinburgh/Leith blending house (est. 1801, John Crabbie & Co). Whisky brand revived by Halewood International in 2018 (8 & 30yo single malts); a Leith micro-distillery was planned. This batch's input brand string 'Crabbie&cree' is unexplained (possibly a scraping artefact merging two catalogue entries) - alias kept verbatim; treated as resolving to Crabbie. Peat/style of the specific revival releases not confirmed, hence unknown.

Unpeated Speyside workhorse malt (Elgin), mainly for blends (Haig, Dimple). First official bottling was Diageo's Flora & Fauna 12yo (1992) - matches this batch's mangled input brand string 'Flora&fauna,mannochmore'.

20-year-old single grain selected by Stephanie Macleod, John Dewar & Sons' Master Blender. Sources are inconsistent on the exact source distillery - one snippet implied Macduff, a malt-only distillery that cannot produce grain whisky, which looks like an error - so the exact distillery is not confirmed and no parentSlug/kind=distillery is given. Grain whisky from a column still is essentially never peated.
Now bottled only as 'Private Stock', Willett's own distillate (formerly a sourced bourbon of undisclosed origin under older Green/Black labels).
Arran's peated line (14-20ppm depending on edition); sibling of the unpeated core 'Arran' brand, same distillery - classic Tobermory/Ledaig-style pair.

column7: Morrison & MacKay (now Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers)
column15: Perth-based independent bottler/blender; brands include Carn Mor and Mac-Talla (single malt) and Old Perth and Bruadar (blends, matches this batch's 'Old Perth' sample). Rebranded 'Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers' in 2020.

Single-barrel cask-strength Kentucky straight bourbon bottled by Augusta Distillery (Augusta, KY), the distillery's inaugural bourbon. Sourced from an undisclosed Kentucky distillery ('rumored' Heaven Hill, not confirmed) so no parentSlug given per the undisclosed-origin rule. No smoke/peat in tasting notes (oak-char notes only).
~12yo small-batch bourbon, part of Willett's Small Batch Boutique Bourbon Collection.

Blend of Highland single malts recreating the character of the Mackinlay's whisky found frozen at Shackleton's Antarctic base camp (barley dried with Orkney peat); described as 'a gentle bite of peat smoke' - a trace, not a peated whisky.
Deliberately smoky blend of Islay (peaty) and Speyside malts; tasting notes describe 'tangy peat' and a 'smoky dram' throughout - more pronounced than a trace.

Colorado-blended American whiskey created by Jess Graber (Stranahan's founder), mash mostly corn/rye. Marketed as 'American Whiskey' rather than 'bourbon' so defaultTypeName left empty rather than forced.
Frankfort, KY. Makes many bourbon/rye brands so defaultTypeName left empty. Added as parent of Blanton's (this batch).

Lawrenceburg, Indiana. Major sourced-whiskey supplier historically (Bulleit, Dickel, Willett, Templeton and others) as well as its own Rossville Union brand. Added as parent of Rossville Union (this batch).

Bardstown, KY. Reopened as an operating distillery in 2012 after decades as a sourcing/bottling operation (Kentucky Bourbon Distillers, 1984-2012). Added as parent of Johnny Drum and Pure Kentucky XO (this batch).
Bardstown, KY. Added as parent of Rittenhouse (this batch).
Lochranza, est. 1995 by ex-Chivas Brothers MD Harold Currie. Unpeated core range (10yo, Bothy, Bodega). Peated sibling line is Machrie Moor (this batch, parentSlug=arran).

'The only remaining Highland distillery to fully peat their standard malt.' Current OB Legacy is an 80% peated / 20% unpeated vatting. Historically the signature malt in Teacher's blend. Named in Artist series samples (this batch).

Closed distillery (mothballed 2000, demolished 2016), Miyota, Nagano Prefecture. Peat level of the original production was not confirmed by the research done here (found only that a newly revived operation reportedly plans both peated and unpeated malt in future) - left unknown rather than guessed. Named in Artist series samples (this batch).
~35-38ppm, comparable to Lagavulin's level - classed heavy rather than medium on that basis. Named in Artist and The Kinship series samples (this batch).
Unpeated malted barley to a tight spec. Named in Artist series samples (this batch).
~25ppm; 'gentle peat' rather than aggressive smoke. Named in Artist, Elements of Islay and The Kinship series samples (this batch).
Unpeated, grassy/floral/orchard-fruit character. Named in Artist series samples (this batch).
Unpeated Islay outlier by design. Peated sibling line is Moine (not in this batch - see brief's own known-pairs list). Named in The Kinship series samples (this batch).
Alness; mainly a blending workhorse, unpeated. Named in Yellow Edition samples (this batch).
Pitlochry; ~95% of output goes into Bell's blend, unpeated. Named in Yellow Edition samples (this batch).
Independent bottler/blender. Other ranges include The Spice King and The Peat Chimney (peated) - not in this batch. Added as bottlerSlug parent of The Hive (this batch).
